acceptance.denominator: 5 of 5 required sections, 3 line-anchored fields, and 1 ASCII sweep over the whole record
acceptance.status_reason: IT FAILED FIRST AND THE FAILURE IS WORTH MORE THAN THE PASS, so it is recorded rather than smoothed away. The first run answered OW-S5-RECORD-FAIL no 'context_keys:' line, while this seat's own grep for the substring had reported it PRESENT. Both were right: the record carried the three fields wrapped in Markdown backticks, and the checker's patterns are LINE-ANCHORED (^context_keys: \S, ^requests_30d: (\d+|NO-METRIC)\b, ^control_portal_api_30d: (\d+)\b), so a line beginning with a backtick satisfies none of them. A substring search and a line-anchored search are different instruments and the looser one agreed with what I wanted to be true. The three lines were unwrapped to column 0, each pattern was then matched directly before re-running the check, and the check passes: 5 of 5 sections, requests_30d=NO-METRIC, control=54824. The ASCII sweep is the checker's own (any ord > 127 fails it) and the record carries 0 non-ASCII characters.

mutant.description: Nothing can be mutated in a read-only act, so the mutant's JOB -- a read whose value differs between the world being one way and the other -- is carried by the PORTAL API CONTROL on the traffic question, which is the one finding here that is an ABSENCE. A zero from CloudWatch can mean no traffic, or a wrong namespace, a wrong dimension name, a wrong window or a denied read. The control is the same namespace, metric, dimension shape, period, statistic and window, pointed at an API that is certainly busy.
mutant.expected: a non-zero total for the portal API 7k3ed8px20 if the query shape and window can see traffic at all; a zero or an error if the instrument is blind, in which case the second API's zero would prove nothing
mutant.observed: the portal API returned 31 datapoints totalling 54824 requests over the same 30 days, and a second control in the Lambda namespace (trade-submission-handler, 7 invocations over 2 datapoints) confirmed the Invocations shape too. So both query shapes see traffic where traffic exists, and the second API's 0 datapoints -- together with list-metrics returning 0 metric rows for it -- is an absence of requests rather than an absence of instrument.

determinism.method: No act was repeated, because nothing was called or changed and a second identical read of a metric window returns the same stored aggregate rather than an independent sample. The comparison used instead is CORROBORATION ACROSS INDEPENDENT INSTRUMENTS: the traffic question was asked three ways that would fail differently -- the existence of the API's Count metric (list-metrics), the metric's datapoints over the window on two different dimension sets, and the Invocations of the two functions that door's routes must pass through -- plus whether the stage keeps an access log that could disagree.
determinism.observed: STABLE: all four agree. list-metrics finds no Count metric for w8jnzvs21g at all; get-metric-statistics returns 0 datapoints with ApiId alone AND with ApiId+Stage=prod; trade-authorizer and trade-auth-handler each show 0 invocations over the same 30 days, which is the stronger reading of the two because every CUSTOM route of that API must invoke the authorizer; and the stage has no access log, so no fourth record exists to contradict them. The code reading corroborates the same conclusion from the other side: the authorizer returns a context of exactly email, name and role, so the two functions released today refuse every caller of this door, which is consistent with a door nothing uses.
